# `kernel/drivers/AmbientOceanSurface.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientOceanSurface.js`

_No file-level description found in source. Add one as a leading `/** ... */` JSDoc comment, or document it below._

## Constants

- `AMBIENT_OCEAN_SURFACE_WGSL` — Independent analytic open-water model, shared by authored wallpaper lanes. Units are metres and seconds. This is a finite directional wave model, not an FFT, shallow-water solver or simulation of shoreline transport. Both visible displacement and normals come from the same filtered height function.
- `AMBIENT_OCEAN_WHITEWATER_WGSL` — Analytic whitewater appearance reconstructed from five recent wave samples. This bounded history is deterministic at any time and needs no retained GPU state. It approximates crest deposition/decay, not SPH or foam transport. Factory compositions persist every function below inside their foam node.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```
